title: Tenbri: the open-source Agent Decision Record
excerpt: An Agent Decision Record is a signed, append-only record of every decision an AI agent makes, verifiable offline by anyone. Tenbri is the open-source one: an audit trail for AI agents, hash-chained and signed, on storage you control.
content_html:
The Agent Decision Record

Proof of what your agents decided

An Agent Decision Record is a signed, append-only record of every decision an AI agent makes: who acted, under which rule and inputs, who approved, and what happened, verifiable offline by anyone. Tenbri is the open-source one. One line for Claude, OpenAI and LangGraph agents; plain files on storage you control.

$ pip install --pre tenbri

Get startedExamplesAdaptersGitHub

import tenbri

tenbri.init()                        # TENBRI_STREAM, TENBRI_AGENT, TENBRI_APPROVER
tenbri.instrument_claude_agent_sdk() # every tool call becomes a signed decision

# or: tenbri.instrument_openai_agents()
# or: tenbri.instrument_langchain()

Tenbri UI

See what your agents decided

tenbrid serves a read-only UI over your streams: dashboards, every decision with its outcome, traces as timelines, and a verification check. Open it with a bearer token; it cannot write.

127.0.0.1:7070

Overview, then the errors, one decision's timeline and signed chain, its whole trace, and the integrity check.

See it run

Record, verify, tamper, get caught

A refund function decorated with @tenbri.decision, called three times. Then someone edits one byte on disk. Real output from a run, with hashes and paths shortened.

  1. 1Record
  2. 2Read
  3. 3Verify
  4. 4Tamper
  5. 5Caught

tenbri quickstart

# create a stream; the CLI records its fingerprint on this machine

$export TENBRI_STREAM=audit/support TENBRI_AGENT=agent:support

$tenbri init

created stream tnb1:986d8e32f69cb7b19e170a65792a3588 at audit/support

stream key fingerprint (pin it): sha256:986d8e32…cd52f52

pinned in ~/demo/keys/pins: tenbri verify audit/support uses it

# refund.py decorates a refund function with @tenbri.decision and calls it three times

$python refund.py

ok: re_123

refused: over the 500 EUR ceiling

error: nothing to refund

# each call wrote an intent before it ran, then its outcome

$tenbri tail -n 6 --no-follow

3 2026-10-20T16:49:42.442Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX - verified

4 2026-10-20T16:49:42.464Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX ok verified

5 2026-10-20T16:49:42.485Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY - verified

6 2026-10-20T16:49:42.504Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY refused verified

7 2026-10-20T16:49:42.525Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_0 - verified

8 2026-10-20T16:49:42.546Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_0 error verified

$tenbri show 4

seq 4 decision outcome 01M5D3G0HWD934QDJNSR0230F8

action issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX

intent 01M5D3G0H716Y40JZR8KTCSXXY

principal agent:support

status ok

verification verified, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

# checks every hash, signature and key against the recorded pin

$tenbri verify

verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

# someone edits one refund on disk

$sed -i '' s/ch_9ZzY/ch_9ZzZ/ audit/support/batches/000000000005.jsonl

# the first changed entry fails verification

$tenbri verify

broken at seq 5: bad_signature: the signature does not verify

4 entries verified before it, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588 (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

OpenAI

Hugging Face

From the blog · Incident analysis

Five days to “it was us”

In July 2026, OpenAI agents broke out of an evaluation sandbox and attacked Hugging Face. Attribution took five days. What a signed record of every agent decision would have changed, and what it would not.

Read the analysis

  1. ~17,600agent actions Hugging Face recovered from its own logs
  2. 5 daysfrom the public disclosure to “it was us”
  3. 1 querywith a Tenbri record: tenbri query --target-domain, on the roadmap

What you get

Built for the day something goes wrong

Disputes, incidents, policy changes and audits all ask the same question: what did the agent decide, and on whose authority?

$ tenbri verify
verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

$ tenbri verify    # after someone edits one batch on disk
broken at seq 5: bad_signature: the signature does not verify
4 entries verified before it, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588

$ tenbri verify audit/support --key sha256:986d8e32…   # an auditor on another machine pins it

Verify

Anyone can check it, offline

Hand an auditor the stream and one fingerprint. Verification checks canonical bytes, the hash chain, every Ed25519 signature and every key, with no access to your systems. A checkpoint they kept catches truncation and forks.

How integrity works 

$ tenbri query --rule policy:refund@14
3  2026-10-20T16:49:42.442Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX  -  verified
5  2026-10-20T16:49:42.485Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY  -  verified
7  2026-10-20T16:49:42.525Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_0     -  verified

$ tenbri query --rule policy:refund@14 --json | jq .entry.action   # JSON when piped

Query

Every decision made under the old rule

Inputs are pinned by reference, version and keyed digest. When a policy changes, list what was decided under the previous version and review it. Each answer is re-checked against storage before it is returned.

Review a policy change 

unknown_actions = "reject"

[actions.issue_refund]
target   = "stripe:{charge}"     # filled from the tool call's arguments
policy   = "policy:refund@14"    # the rule that allowed it
approval = true                  # a person must approve first
inputs   = ["policy:refund"]

[actions.issue_refund.fields."ext.refund.amount"]
required = true
type = "integer"

Schemas

Say what each action must record

Declare actions once in tenbri.toml. The SDKs read it to map tool calls to actions, targets and policies, tenbrid enforces it at write time, and CI checks whole streams against it.

Action schemas 

$ tenbri receipt create ./audit/support --entry 3 --out refund-3.receipt
$ tenbri receipt verify refund-3.receipt --key sha256:9c1e…
proves seq 3 (decision intent), id 01M4XBH0Y6…, ts 2026-10-14T14:02:13Z (claimed by the writer)
in stream tnb1:1702…b7d8, checkpoint at size 8, pinned to sha256:9c1e…; key history: 2 key entries

Receipts

Proof you can hand over

A receipt proves specific entries with their inclusion proofs, the key history and an optional RFC 3161 timestamp. A customer, a regulator or the police verify it alone, without seeing the rest of the stream.

Receipts and timestamps 

$ tenbri erase ./audit/support --subject subj_7f3c91d2 --reason dsr:2026-1042 --yes
erased subject subj_7f3c91d2: 2 data key epochs deleted; erasure recorded at seq 7

$ tenbri verify ./audit/support --key sha256:9c1e…
verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:1702…b7d8, pinned to sha256:9c1e…

Privacy

Erase a person without breaking the chain

Only hashes go in the chain. Bodies are encrypted and input digests are keyed per subject, so deleting a subject's keys makes their data unreadable while every chain, checkpoint and receipt still verifies.

Privacy and erasure 

$ export TENBRI_STREAM=r2://audit/agents/support CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=…

$ curl -X POST https://tenbrid.internal:7070/v1/streams/support/intents \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(ulid)" \
    -d '{"action":{"type":"issue_refund","target":"stripe:ch_81f2"}}'
{"entry":{"kind":"decision","phase":"intent","seq":3,…},"replayed":false}

Anywhere

Your storage, any language

A stream is plain files in a directory, S3, R2 or MinIO, with the keys kept apart. Write from Python, TypeScript or Rust, or run tenbrid and use REST or gRPC from anything else.

tenbrid API

A new kind of record

Logs, traces, decision records

Observability tools such as Langfuse and MLflow answer how an agent ran. A decision record proves what it decided and on whose authority. Keep both: Tenbri links each decision to its OpenTelemetry trace.

QuestionLogsTracesDecision records
What it answersWhat a service printedHow the agent ran: steps, latency, tokens, costWhat the agent decided, and on whose authority
Who it servesOperatorsEngineers improving the agentAuditors, customers, regulators and incident review
Can it be altered?Yes: edited, rotated, deletedYes: sampled, rewritten, expiredNo: any change fails verification
Can a third party verify it?No, they must trust youNo, they need your accountYes, offline, with one fingerprint

Architecture

Write, sign and chain, store, prove

One Rust core behind every SDK, the CLI and tenbrid. Turn on the optional parts when you need them; the rest is on the roadmap.

Records these frameworks ask for

Evidence, not screenshots

Tenbri gives you the records. It does not make a system compliant on its own.

  • EU AI Act Art. 12, 14, 19, 26
  • GDPR Art. 22
  • DORA
  • NIS2
  • SOC 2
  • ISO/IEC 27001
  • ISO/IEC 42001
  • NIST AI RMF

Start recording decisions in five minutes

Open source, Apache-2.0, written in Rust. Plain files on storage you control, and no telemetry.

content_html_zh:
The Agent Decision Record

Proof of what your agents decided

An Agent Decision Record is a signed, append-only record of every decision an AI agent makes: who acted, under which rule and inputs, who approved, and what happened, verifiable offline by anyone. Tenbri is the open-source one. One line for Claude, OpenAI and LangGraph agents; plain files on storage you control.

$ pip install --pre tenbri

Get startedExamplesAdaptersGitHub

import tenbri

tenbri.init()                        # TENBRI_STREAM, TENBRI_AGENT, TENBRI_APPROVER
tenbri.instrument_claude_agent_sdk() # every tool call becomes a signed decision

# or: tenbri.instrument_openai_agents()
# or: tenbri.instrument_langchain()

Tenbri UI

See what your agents decided

tenbrid serves a read-only UI over your streams: dashboards, every decision with its outcome, traces as timelines, and a verification check. Open it with a bearer token; it cannot write.

127.0.0.1:7070

Overview, then the errors, one decision's timeline and signed chain, its whole trace, and the integrity check.

看到它运行

Record, verify, tamper, get caught

A refund function decorated with @tenbri.decision, called three times. Then someone edits one byte on disk. Real output from a run, with hashes and paths shortened.

  1. 1Record
  2. 2Read
  3. 3Verify
  4. 4Tamper
  5. 5Caught

tenbri quickstart

# create a stream; the CLI records its fingerprint on this machine

$export TENBRI_STREAM=audit/support TENBRI_AGENT=agent:support

$tenbri init

created stream tnb1:986d8e32f69cb7b19e170a65792a3588 at audit/support

stream key fingerprint (pin it): sha256:986d8e32…cd52f52

pinned in ~/demo/keys/pins: tenbri verify audit/support uses it

# refund.py decorates a refund function with @tenbri.decision and calls it three times

$python refund.py

ok: re_123

refused: over the 500 EUR ceiling

error: nothing to refund

# each call wrote an intent before it ran, then its outcome

$tenbri tail -n 6 --no-follow

3 2026-10-20T16:49:42.442Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX - verified

4 2026-10-20T16:49:42.464Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX ok verified

5 2026-10-20T16:49:42.485Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY - verified

6 2026-10-20T16:49:42.504Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY refused verified

7 2026-10-20T16:49:42.525Z decision intent agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_0 - verified

8 2026-10-20T16:49:42.546Z decision outcome agent:support issue_refund stripe:ch_0 error verified

$tenbri show 4

seq 4 decision outcome 01M5D3G0HWD934QDJNSR0230F8

action issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX

intent 01M5D3G0H716Y40JZR8KTCSXXY

principal agent:support

status ok

verification verified, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

# checks every hash, signature and key against the recorded pin

$tenbri verify

verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

# someone edits one refund on disk

$sed -i '' s/ch_9ZzY/ch_9ZzZ/ audit/support/batches/000000000005.jsonl

# the first changed entry fails verification

$tenbri verify

broken at seq 5: bad_signature: the signature does not verify

4 entries verified before it, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588 (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

开放人工智能

抱脸

From the blog · Incident analysis

Five days to “it was us”

In July 2026, OpenAI agents broke out of an evaluation sandbox and attacked Hugging Face. Attribution took five days. What a signed record of every agent decision would have changed, and what it would not.

Read the analysis

  1. ~17,600agent actions Hugging Face recovered from its own logs
  2. 5 daysfrom the public disclosure to “it was us”
  3. 1 querywith a Tenbri record: tenbri query --target-domain, on the roadmap

你得到什么

Built for the day something goes wrong

Disputes, incidents, policy changes and audits all ask the same question: what did the agent decide, and on whose authority?

$ tenbri verify
verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588, pinned to sha256:986d8e32… (the pin recorded in ~/demo/keys/pins)

$ tenbri verify    # after someone edits one batch on disk
broken at seq 5: bad_signature: the signature does not verify
4 entries verified before it, stream tnb1:986d8e32…3588

$ tenbri verify audit/support --key sha256:986d8e32…   # an auditor on another machine pins it

核实

Anyone can check it, offline

Hand an auditor the stream and one fingerprint. Verification checks canonical bytes, the hash chain, every Ed25519 signature and every key, with no access to your systems. A checkpoint they kept catches truncation and forks.

How integrity works

$ tenbri query --rule policy:refund@14
3  2026-10-20T16:49:42.442Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_3PqX  -  verified
5  2026-10-20T16:49:42.485Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_9ZzY  -  verified
7  2026-10-20T16:49:42.525Z  decision intent  agent:support  issue_refund stripe:ch_0     -  verified

$ tenbri query --rule policy:refund@14 --json | jq .entry.action   # JSON when piped

Query

Every decision made under the old rule

Inputs are pinned by reference, version and keyed digest. When a policy changes, list what was decided under the previous version and review it. Each answer is re-checked against storage before it is returned.

Review a policy change

unknown_actions = "reject"

[actions.issue_refund]
target   = "stripe:{charge}"     # filled from the tool call's arguments
policy   = "policy:refund@14"    # the rule that allowed it
approval = true                  # a person must approve first
inputs   = ["policy:refund"]

[actions.issue_refund.fields."ext.refund.amount"]
required = true
type = "integer"

Schemas

Say what each action must record

Declare actions once in tenbri.toml. The SDKs read it to map tool calls to actions, targets and policies, tenbrid enforces it at write time, and CI checks whole streams against it.

Action schemas

$ tenbri receipt create ./audit/support --entry 3 --out refund-3.receipt
$ tenbri receipt verify refund-3.receipt --key sha256:9c1e…
proves seq 3 (decision intent), id 01M4XBH0Y6…, ts 2026-10-14T14:02:13Z (claimed by the writer)
in stream tnb1:1702…b7d8, checkpoint at size 8, pinned to sha256:9c1e…; key history: 2 key entries

Receipts

Proof you can hand over

A receipt proves specific entries with their inclusion proofs, the key history and an optional RFC 3161 timestamp. A customer, a regulator or the police verify it alone, without seeing the rest of the stream.

Receipts and timestamps

$ tenbri erase ./audit/support --subject subj_7f3c91d2 --reason dsr:2026-1042 --yes
erased subject subj_7f3c91d2: 2 data key epochs deleted; erasure recorded at seq 7

$ tenbri verify ./audit/support --key sha256:9c1e…
verified 8 entries, stream tnb1:1702…b7d8, pinned to sha256:9c1e…

隐私

Erase a person without breaking the chain

Only hashes go in the chain. Bodies are encrypted and input digests are keyed per subject, so deleting a subject's keys makes their data unreadable while every chain, checkpoint and receipt still verifies.

Privacy and erasure

$ export TENBRI_STREAM=r2://audit/agents/support CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=…

$ curl -X POST https://tenbrid.internal:7070/v1/streams/support/intents \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(ulid)" \
    -d '{"action":{"type":"issue_refund","target":"stripe:ch_81f2"}}'
{"entry":{"kind":"decision","phase":"intent","seq":3,…},"replayed":false}

Anywhere

Your storage, any language

A stream is plain files in a directory, S3, R2 or MinIO, with the keys kept apart. Write from Python, TypeScript or Rust, or run tenbrid and use REST or gRPC from anything else.

tenbrid API

A new kind of record

Logs, traces, decision records

Observability tools such as Langfuse and MLflow answer how an agent ran. A decision record proves what it decided and on whose authority. Keep both: Tenbri links each decision to its OpenTelemetry trace.
